signature.name: Ten-second read
signature.description: Can every word of visible copy on the first screen be read in about ten seconds, with nothing cuttable?

group-a.signature_why: Headline is plain, but 'drawn a number' plus 'sold out like our 9am country loaf' is two puns where none were needed, and an Hours button that jumps to hours already shown.
group-a.loved: 'We can't find that page.' leads, with hours bolded directly under it.
group-a.docked: Pun stack in the body line and a ticket 'No.' that makes the reader decode 4-loaf-4.

group-b.signature_why: Tightest first screen: headline, one line, status, three buttons; still says 'sold out' and 'nothing in the oven' for the same idea, and repeats the path twice.
group-b.loved: Visitor's own typo on the loaf is the only clever thing and it costs zero words of explanation.
group-b.docked: Lead line doubles its metaphor; hours appear in both the status and the Hours button.

group-c.signature_why: Most copy of the three: headline, handwritten echo, tagline, a lead-in sentence, button sublabels, a sign-off and a margin note; half could go.
group-c.loved: Plain 'Page not found' plus the week table with today marked is genuinely useful.
group-c.docked: Strikes through a path it replaced with 'this page' at /menue.html, so the 'we looked for this line' sentence points at nothing.
